segments.t: A big football match is on, and Barinov wants to watch it in peace. Senya tells him that the owner is calling for him, urgently. Listen to who says what.
Сеня, не мешай мне смотреть футбол!
Шеф, вас срочно зовёт Дмитрий Владимирович!
Почему хозяин звонит именно в этот момент?
Он сказал, что это очень срочное дело.
Я знаю этого человека целых двадцать лет.
Он ждёт вас прямо сейчас возле зала.
Наша команда ведёт в счёте два ноль!
Я обещаю внимательно следить за счётом.
Если наша команда проиграет, я накажу тебя!
Шеф, я не отойду от экрана телевизора.
Ладно, я пойду и выслушаю Дмитрия Владимировича.
Удачи вам в разговоре с хозяином!
Смотри в оба и внимательно следи за счётом!
Let's take the lines one by one.

не

'Senya, don't disturb me watching football!' The speaker uses 'disturb' means both 'to stir', as in Louis's earlier line, and 'to disturb', as here. The phrase means 'don't disturb me'. The speaker uses 'to watch football' is also included.
Шеф, вас срочно зовёт Дмитрий Владимирович!
зовёт
'Chef, Dmitry Vladimirovich is urgently calling you!' The word means 'calls', to summon someone, from the action word of Senya's earlier line. Senya uses the owner's first name and father's name.
Почему хозяин звонит именно в этот момент?
хозяин
'Why does the owner call at this exact moment?' The word is 'owner' or 'master', heard in Vika's earlier line. The phrase means 'exactly at this moment'. Barinov is annoyed.
Он сказал, что это очень срочное дело.
срочное
дело
'He said that this is a very urgent matter.' The phrase means 'urgent matter', the words Max used to escape from Vika. The other word means 'he said'.

'I have known this man for a whole twenty years.' Barinov says 'I know': twenty years and still counting. After the word for twenty, Notice the part 'years' is used. The other word means 'whole', for emphasis.

ждёт
вас
'He is waiting for you right now near the hall.' This phrase means 'waits you', leaving out 'for'. The next phrase means 'near the hall'. In Russian, 'right now' translates is also included.

'Our team is leading in the score two-nil!' The phrase means 'leads in the score'; the action Here, 'to lead' shows is also the action word used for 'to behave'. Here, 'two-nil' shows is also here.
Я обещаю внимательно следить за счётом.
следить
за
'I promise to watch the score carefully.' The phrase means 'to keep an eye on', the action word in Barinov's earlier line. The other word means 'I promise', as in Louis's earlier line.
Если наша команда проиграет, я накажу тебя!
проиграет
'If our team loses, I will punish you!' The word means 'loses', the word from the first scene. The other word means 'I will punish'.
Шеф, я не отойду от экрана телевизора.
отойду

'Chef, I will not step away from the TV screen.' The word means 'I will step away', as in Barinov's earlier line. The phrase means 'from the screen': Listen to how 'screen' gets an ending after the connecting word.
Ладно, я пойду и выслушаю Дмитрия Владимировича.
выслушаю

'Fine, I will go and hear Dmitry Vladimirovich out.' The word means 'I will hear out': a starting bit on the action The speaker uses 'to listen' means 'to the end'. After it, the name changes form. The football will have to wait.
